title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
summary: The analyzer crashed when a type had repeated keys, or mixed integer and string keys. The AI changed TypeCollector.cs so the analyzer reports MsgPack005 instead. It keeps the first member for each key, and skips a member with the wrong key kind once it is reported. It also added analyzer tests, execution tests and a README section on opting out of source generation.
head: 9007cee1

claims.claim: The analyzer no longer crashes on duplicate integer keys, duplicate string keys or mixed key kinds. It reports MsgPack005 instead, with or without SuppressSourceGeneration.
claims.why_this_tier: 4 new tests fail before the change, because the analyzer crashes (AD0001) next to the MsgPack005. They pass after.

claims.claim: After the change, the real TypeCollector never throws on any list of 1 to 4 keyed members with integer or string keys. Before the change, it threw on most of them.
claims.why_this_tier: A formal model, written in Dafny, proves this for lists of any length. The model matches the real C# code on every input up to 4 members. The real code throws before the change and not after. The weakest step is a test, so the claim counts as Tested.

chain.link: The Dafny model proves BranchNeverFailsForIntAndStringKeys with no unproven assumptions.
The model matches the real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs, before and after the change, with 0 mismatches.

claims.claim: The fix is incomplete. If a type's first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)], the analyzer still crashes (AD0001, ArgumentNullException). This also happens with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
claims.why_this_tier: An experiment on the real analyzer shows the crash before and after the change. That is a gap, not a passing check, so it cannot count as Tested and the owner decides.

claims.claim: The change hides a diagnostic. The new `continue` also skips collecting the member's type. So a member with a mixed key and an unserializable type no longer gets MsgPack003. Before the change, it got MsgPack003 when the first key was a string.
claims.why_this_tier: It drops a diagnostic the old code reported. Whether that is fine, given the same member already gets the MsgPack005 error, is a product decision.

claims.claim: Every repeated key is reported. When two members share a key, the first one is kept and the second gets MsgPack005 ('must be unique').
claims.why_this_tier: The duplicate-key tests fail before the change and pass after. The model's proof DupReported matches the real C# code on every input up to 4 members.

chain.link: The Dafny model proves DupReported: the first member wins and every repeat is reported.
The model matches the real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs.
The duplicate-key tests fail before the change and pass after.

claims.claim: The fix is copied into both the properties loop and the fields loop, which adds duplicate code to TypeCollector.cs.
claims.why_this_tier: The numbers come from a script that measures duplicate code and complexity, run before and after the change.

claims.claim: 4 of the 8 new analyzer tests already pass before the change, so they guard old behaviour and do not show the fix works. They cover a missing key, AllowPrivate, the member type and generation-only diagnostics.
claims.why_this_tier: The count comes from running the tests before and after the change.

claims.claim: A type with SuppressSourceGeneration gets no generated formatter, and still round-trips through the run-time (dynamic) resolver. The 2 new execution tests are meant to show this.
claims.why_this_tier: The tests never ran. Their project does not build here, before or after the change, because the source generator does not load (CS9057).

claims.claim: The new README section says the analyzer still checks suppressed types for MsgPack003, 004, 005, 012 and 015, and skips MsgPack011, 016 and 017 for them.
claims.why_this_tier: It is documentation. Tests cover 003, 004, 005, 015 and the skipped ones, but not 012. And C-2234-03 shows a case where the MsgPack005 check still crashes.

found: We found (probe, real analyzer): the new `continue` skips CollectCore for the member's type, so MsgPack003 is lost for a mixed-key member (C-2234-04).

We found (probe, real analyzer, Dafny model): a first field with [Key(null)] still crashes the analyzer with ArgumentNullException, on base and branch, with SuppressSourceGeneration too. The properties loop guards with `else if (stringKey is not null)`; the fields loop uses a bare `else` (C-2234-03).

The theorem in the brief ('collecting keys never fails, whatever keys repeat or mix kinds') is false for the real code. Dafny proves the exact condition instead: it fails if and only if the first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)].
Finding (b) dropped: the second member of a repeated key gets MsgPack005 on the branch, and the first one is kept (C-2234-05).

The base crash on repeated keys also happens without SuppressSourceGeneration (test DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes fails on base). The bug is not specific to suppressed types, and 4 of the 8 analyzer tests show the analyzer already validated suppressed types on base.
SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs raises StyleCop SA1649 (file name does not match first type name).
Pre-existing, outside the diff: the fields-loop BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic passes no message arguments, so the message reads 'Both int and string keys are null: {0}.{1}'.

refused.what: C-2234-04: the `continue` drops MsgPack003 for mixed-key members
refused.why: Dropping a diagnostic that base reported is a product call for the analyzer owner.

scope_drift: README.md gains a 14-line 'Opting out of source generation' section. The issue title asks for an analyzer fix, not documentation.
not_checked: The 2 execution tests (SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs): the project does not build here because the generator needs compiler 4.12 and SDK 8.0.402 has 4.11 (CS9057).
Source generator output (reportDiagnostic is null in the generator path) for repeated or mixed keys: what code is emitted when the first member wins.
MsgPack012 (inaccessible types) for suppressed types, which the README claims.
The full test suite on the branch; only the new tests and our probes were run.
Members without any [Key] attribute, inherited members, records with positional parameters: not in the model's input domain.
The model's input domain is keys 0, 1, "a", "b" and null, with up to 4 members, so the model-vs-C# check covers 3710 inputs, not all inputs.
The issue body: only the issue title was available to us.
